examples.en: It's just an abrasion and a bruise. Nothing's broken.
This ankle abrasion is still sore.

abstain.definition: v. refrain from voting\nv. choose not to consume
abstain.translation: vi. 自制, 戒绝, 弃权, 回避

examples.en: I had to abstain from smoking while I was in the hospital.
examples.zh: 在医院的时候，我不得不戒烟。

examples.en: My father tries to abstain from drinking.
examples.zh: 我父亲正在尝试戒酒。

examples.en: Tom abstained from voting.
examples.zh: 汤姆投票弃权。

abstraction.definition:
n. a concept or idea not associated with any specific instance
n. the act of withdrawing or removing something
n. the process of formulating general concepts by abstracting common properties of instances
n. an abstract painting
abstraction.translation: n. 抽象化, 心不在焉, 空想, 提炼, 抽象派作品\n[化] 提取; 抽取; 夺取; 夺取反应; 除去

examples.en: This whole matter is a mere abstraction for you.
Fascists are enabled by liberals' preference for abstractions over people.
This is an example of abstraction.

accessory.definition:
n. clothing that is worn or carried, but not part of your main clothing
n. a supplementary component that improves capability
n. someone who helps another person commit a crime
s. furnishing added support
accessory.translation: n. 附件, 零件, 附加物, 从犯, 同谋\na. 附属的, 补充的, 同谋的, 帮凶的, 非主要的, 副的\n[计] 附件

examples.en: Do you sell coffee pot accessories too?
examples.zh: 你们也有贩售咖啡壶配件吗？

examples.en: By the 1940s, the qipao came in a wide variety of designs and fabrics, with an equally wide variety of accessories.
examples.zh: 到了四十年代，旗袍有了种类繁多的图案和面料，也有了同样种类繁多的饰品。

acclaim.translation: n. 喝彩, 欢呼, 赞同\nv. 欢呼, 喝彩, 称赞

examples.en: She was a brilliant scholar, receiving acclaim far and wide.
Adriano's star performance at the theater won him critical acclaim.
The band's final album was met with universal acclaim.

acne.definition: n. an inflammatory disease involving the sebaceous glands of the skin; characterized by papules or pustules or comedones
acne.translation: n. 痤疮, 粉刺\n[医] 痤疮, 粉刺

examples.en: Oliver has an acne problem.
examples.zh: 奥利弗有粉刺。

acorn.definition: n. fruit of the oak tree: a smooth thin-walled nut in a woody cup-shaped base
acorn.translation: n. 橡树果实\n[机] 浆栎, 浆栎果

examples.en: From a small acorn grows a tall oak tree.
examples.zh: 一粒小小的橡实可以长成一棵高大的橡树。

examples.en: This recipe requires acorn squash.
examples.zh: 这个菜谱需要一些青南瓜。

examples.en: A hungry pig dreams of acorns.
examples.zh: 饥饿的猪梦到橡树子。

acronym.definition: n. a word formed from the initial letters of the several words in the name
acronym.translation: n. 首字母缩拼词, 首字母组合词\n[计] 字首组合词

examples.en: Who can tell me what the acronym Tatoeba stands for?
examples.zh: 谁能告诉我TATOEBA首字母缩合词的意思？

addict.definition: n. someone who is so ardently devoted to something that it resembles an addiction\nn. someone who is physiologically dependent on a substance; abrupt deprivation of the substance produces withdrawal symptoms\nv. to cause (someone or oneself) to become dependent (on something, especially a narcotic drug)
addict.translation: vt. 使沉溺, 使上瘾\nn. 入迷的人, 上瘾者

examples.en: Many criminals in the United States are addicted to drugs.
examples.zh: 美国的罪犯大多是吸毒成瘾的瘾君子。

examples.en: Wan-chun’s a total drama addict — Korean, American, she watches them all.
examples.zh: 婉君超爱追剧，韩剧、美剧她都看。

examples.en: Many criminals in America are addicted to drugs.
examples.zh: 美国的罪犯大多是吸毒成瘾的瘾君子。

adhesive.translation: a. 粘着的, 涂有粘性物质的\nn. 粘合剂, 橡皮膏

examples.en: Scotch brand is a type of adhesive tape.
She secured the edges of her crafts with her trusty adhesive tape.
It is covered with adhesives from many distant countries.
The living room adjoins the dining room.
examples.zh: 客厅紧邻著餐厅。

examples.en: Germany adjoins the Netherlands.
examples.zh: 德国毗邻荷兰。

administrative.definition: a. of or relating to or responsible for administration
administrative.translation: a. 管理的, 行政的\n[法] 行政的, 管理的, 遗产管理的

examples.en: Who is the Administrative Assistant?
examples.zh: 谁是行政助理？

examples.en: The emergence of a third gender has added legal and administrative complications, creating unnecessary burdens.
examples.zh: 第三性别的出现增加了法律和行政上的麻烦，徒增无谓的负担。

admirable.definition: s. deserving of the highest esteem or admiration\ns. inspiring admiration or approval
admirable.translation: a. 可钦佩的, 极好的, 令人惊奇的

examples.en: It is at night that faith in light is admirable.
Nowadays, wisdom no longer appears to be an admirable virtue.
Your motive was admirable, but your action was not.

adorn.definition: v make more attractive by adding ornament, colour, etc.\nv be beautiful to look at\nv furnish with power or authority; of kings or emperors

examples.en: The crown is adorned with dozens of divinely lustrous gemstones.
examples.zh: 王冠上镶嵌著数十颗光彩夺目的宝石。

examples.en: A vase of frost-bleached ferns and ruby-red maple leaves adorned the table.
examples.zh: 桌上摆放著一瓶被霜冻漂白的蕨类植物和红宝石色的枫叶。

advent.definition: n. arrival that has been awaited (especially of something momentous)\nn. the season including the four Sundays preceding Christmas

examples.en: The tribe wasn't delighted about the advent of the peacemaker.
A chocolate is hidden behind each door of this Advent calendar.
Carriages gradually disappeared with the advent of the motorcar.

adversary.translation: n. 敌手, 对手\na. 敌手的, 敌对的

examples.en: Fear is an adversary that one must face to move forward.
Is Russia a strategic partner for us, or a geopolitical adversary?
He received oaths of fealty from all his humbled adversaries.

adversity.definition: n. a state of misfortune or affliction\nn. a stroke of ill fortune; a calamitous event
adversity.translation: n. 逆境, 不幸, 灾祸, 灾难

examples.en: Adversity makes a man wise, not rich.
examples.zh: 逆境出人才。

examples.en: We must learn to meet adversity gracefully.
examples.zh: 我们必须学会优雅地面对逆境。

examples.en: Despite adversity, the architect achieved worldwide fame.
examples.zh: 尽管有逆境，建筑师还是获得了享誉全球的荣誉。

aesthetic.definition:
n. (philosophy) a philosophical theory as to what is beautiful
a. relating to or dealing with the subject of aesthetics
a. concerning or characterized by an appreciation of beauty or good taste
s. aesthetically pleasing
aesthetic.translation: a. 美学的, 审美的, 有美感的

examples.en: I look at it from an aesthetic point of view.
Builders often use granite for its strength and aesthetic appeal.
Tom strives to promote the development of Merry's aesthetic taste.

affectionate.definition: s. having or displaying warmth or affection
affectionate.translation: a. 深情的, 充满情爱的

examples.en: My father was no less affectionate and tender to me than my mother was.
examples.zh: 我爸爸对我的爱和照顾不比我妈妈少。

affiliate.definition: n. a subordinate or subsidiary associate; a person who is affiliated with another or with an organization\nn. a subsidiary or subordinate organization that is affiliated with another organization\nv. join in an affiliation
affiliate.translation: vt. 使紧密联系, 使附属, 接纳, 收养\nvi. 发生联系, 参加

examples.en: Our company and its affiliates may share your personal information with each other.
examples.zh: 我们公司与其分公司会共享你的个人信息。

affirmative.definition: n. a reply of affirmation\na. affirming or giving assent\ns. expecting the best
affirmative.translation: a. 肯定的, 赞成的, 积极的\nn. 肯定语

examples.en: I think I can answer that in the affirmative.
Of all affirmative answers, the simplest one is yes.
Debate is an academic game between the affirmative and the negative.

afflict.definition: v. cause great unhappiness for; distress\nv. cause physical pain or suffering in

examples.en: I will be afflicted that I do not know men.
Her sickness, she is the only one afflicted by it.
Their sickness, they are the only ones afflicted by it.

affluent.definition: n. an affluent person; a person who is financially well off\ns. having an abundant supply of money or possessions of value
affluent.translation: a. 丰富的, 富裕的\nn. 支流, 富人

examples.en: Humanity is now affluent due to progression in science and technology.
examples.zh: 由于科学技术的进步，人类现在很富裕。

aftermath.definition: n. the consequences of an event (especially a catastrophic event)
aftermath.translation: n. 结果, 后果\n[法] 后果, 结果

examples.en: In the aftermath of the accident he lost his sight.
Antonio was still alive in the aftermath of the explosion.
He cried thinking about his ordeal and its unending aftermath.

aggression.definition:
n. a disposition to behave aggressively
n. a feeling of hostility that arouses thoughts of attack
n. violent action that is hostile and usually unprovoked
n. the act of initiating hostilities
aggression.translation: n. 侵犯, 侵略\n[医] 攻击

examples.en: As North Korea displays aggression, South Korea concentrates its forces near the border.
examples.zh: 韩国随着朝鲜的外患而在边界附近集结军队。

examples.en: Russia started its illegal and unjustifiable war of aggression against Ukraine, and Russia can end it.
examples.zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰发动了非法、不公义的侵略战争，而俄罗斯应该终止这一切。

agile.definition: s. moving quickly and lightly\ns. mentally quick
agile.translation: a. 敏捷的, 灵活的, 机敏的

examples.en: Tom is agile.
examples.zh: 汤姆很敏捷。

agonize.definition: v. cause to agonize\nv. suffer agony or anguish
agonize.translation: vt. 使极度痛苦, 折磨\nvi. 感到痛苦

examples.en: I hope we didn't agonize over this decision for nothing.
You just messed up once. You don't need to agonize over it.
We agonized over the decision to do that.

ailment.definition: n. an often persistent bodily disorder or disease; a cause for complaining
ailment.translation: n. 病痛, 疾病\n[医] 疾病

examples.en: Johnny Depp's daughter is reportedly recovering from an unspecified serious ailment.
The doctor said that this ailment is incurable.
The doctor immediately began to look for the cause of Boldi's ailment.

aisle.definition: n. a long narrow passage (as in a cave or woods)\nn. passageway between seating areas as in an auditorium or passenger vehicle or between areas of shelves of goods as in stores\nn. part of a church divided laterally from the nave proper by rows of pillars or columns
aisle.translation: n. 走廊, 侧廊, 过道\n[机] 走道

examples.en: Would you like a window or aisle seat?
examples.zh: 你想靠窗还是走廊？

examples.en: I'd like an aisle seat, please.
examples.zh: 请给我靠走道的位子。

alchemy.definition: n. a pseudoscientific forerunner of chemistry in medieval times
alchemy.translation: n. 炼金术, 魔力\n[化] 炼丹术; 炼金术; 金丹术

examples.en: Love is a perfect alchemy of mind, body, and soul.
Many tales of alchemy show up in "Journey to the West".
Psychoanalysis is to psychology as alchemy is to chemistry.

ale.definition: n. a general name for beer made with a top fermenting yeast; in some of the United States an ale is (by law) a brew of more than 4% alcohol by volume
ale.translation: n. 麦芽酒\n[医] 麦芽酒

examples.en: Pale ale is a low-alcohol beer.
examples.zh: 淡啤酒是一种酒精含量低的啤酒。

alleviate.definition: v provide physical relief, as from pain\nv make easier

examples.en: This kind of medicine can temporarily alleviate pain. If you need it, just take it.
examples.zh: 这种药可以暂时缓解身体的疼痛，你需要的话就拿去吧。

examples.en: In order to alleviate employment pressures, the nation has established a series of relevant policies.
examples.zh: 为了缓解就业压力，国家已经制定了一系列相关政策。

allot.definition: v give out\nv allow to have\nv administer or bestow, as in small portions
allot.translation: vt. 分配, 分摊指定\n[经] (按股或按规定)分配, 配(拨)给, 规(派)定

examples.en: Let's see how much time they allot you.
They allotted to each player the benefits due him.
I go down before my allotted term of life is over.

allowable.definition: s. deductible according to the tax laws\ns. deserving to be allowed or considered
allowable.translation: a. 允许的, 许可的, 容许的\n[经] 允许产量

allude.definition: v. make a more or less disguised reference to

examples.en: I am not alluding to any person in particular.
Miss Ashton never alluded to what had passed in the state-room.
I never alluded to an intent to marry.

allure.definition: n. the power to entice or attract through personal charm
allure.translation: vt. 引诱, 吸引\nn. 魅力, 诱惑力

examples.en: I will never understand the allure of wealth.
He gave himself up to her allure.
Which painting is more alluring, Madame X or the Mona Lisa?

almond.definition: n. small bushy deciduous tree native to Asia and North Africa having pretty pink blossoms and highly prized edible nuts enclosed in a hard green hull; cultivated in southern Australia and California\nn. oval-shaped edible seed of the almond tree

examples.en: Without bee pollination, California's almond crop, for example, would be non-existent.
examples.zh: 例如，如果没有蜜蜂授粉，加州的杏仁作物就不会存在。

examples.en: Add the honey, lemon juice, chopped almonds and the chopped apples.
examples.zh: 加入蜂蜜，柠檬汁，切碎的杏仁和切碎的苹果。

examples.en: The almond trees are in bloom.
examples.zh: 杏树正在开花。

aloft.definition:
r. at or on or to the masthead or upper rigging of a ship
r. upward
r. at or to great height; high up in or into the air
r. in the higher atmosphere above the earth

examples.en: I saw a flock of birds flying aloft.
He stood there with the poker held aloft.
They marched to Santiago with their flag aloft.

amass.definition: v collect or gather\nv get or gather together

examples.en: He amassed a fortune in stock trading during the last boom.
examples.zh: 他在上个景气时期炒股攒下了一笔钱。

examples.en: He amassed a large fortune before he died.
examples.zh: 他死前累积了庞大的财富。

ambient.translation: a. 周围的\nn. 周围环境

examples.en: The soundtracks of most video games are mostly ambient music.
The ambient music made her fly into a rage.
My brother listens to a music genre called ambient.

ambivalent.definition: s. uncertain or unable to decide about what course to follow
ambivalent.translation: a. 矛盾的, 模棱两可的\n[医] 矛盾情绪的

examples.en: He is genuinely ambivalent about running for president again.
India is fairly ambivalent on the Ukraine War.
I have this ambivalent attitude towards my boss.

anatomy.definition: n. the branch of morphology that deals with the structure of animals\nn. a detailed analysis
anatomy.translation: n. 剖析, 解剖学, 骨骼, 结构\n[医] 解剖学, 解剖

examples.en: She studied the bat's anatomy for her biology project.
examples.zh: 她为了完成生物学作业，研究了蝙蝠的解剖构造。

examples.en: Dan didn't even take basic anatomy classes.
examples.zh: 丹甚至没有上过基础解剖课。

anecdote.definition: n. short account of an incident (especially a biographical one)

examples.en: Do you remember the anecdote the captain told yesterday afternoon?
Can you tell me the meaning of this anecdote?
She is more influenced by personal anecdote than I.

angular.definition: a. measured by an angle or by the rate of change of an angle\na. having angles or an angular shape
angular.translation: a. 有角的, 消瘦的, 有尖角的, 生硬的\n[医] 角的, 角形的

examples.en: Her coloring book lay limp, jagged with angular pink scribbles.
This is due to conservation of angular momentum.
An envelope is usually angular and thin.

animate.definition: v. give new life or energy to\na. belonging to the class of nouns that denote living beings\na. endowed with animal life as distinguished from plant life
animate.translation: vt. 使有生气, 赋予生命\na. 有生命的, 有生气的

examples.en: The soul animates the body.
examples.zh: 灵魂赋予肉体生命。

annex.definition: n. an addition that extends a main building\nv. take (territory) as if by conquest\nv. attach to
annex.translation: n. 附加物, 附属建筑物\nvt. 附加, 盖(印), 并吞

examples.en: The annex is on the north of the original building.
Netanyahu's new government is considering to annex the West Bank.
Netanyahu wants to annex the entire territory of the West Bank.

annotate.definition: v. add explanatory notes to or supply with critical comments
annotate.translation: v. 作注解, 注释\n[计] 注释

examples.en: He annotated the book with important notes.
They annotated their textbooks with colored pens.

annoyance.definition: n. anger produced by some annoying irritation\nn. something or someone that causes trouble; a source of unhappiness\nn. the act of troubling or annoying someone
annoyance.translation: n. 烦恼, 打扰, 可厌之事\n[法] 使人烦恼的事物, 麻烦事, 讨厌物

examples.en: To our great annoyance, he barged in on our party.
Focus on the bigger picture and ignore this minor annoyance.
Tom had a look of annoyance on his face.

antecedent.definition: n. a preceding occurrence or cause or event\nn. anything that precedes something similar in time\nn. the referent of an anaphor; a phrase or clause that is referred to by an anaphoric pronoun
antecedent.translation: n. 前情, 先行词\na. 先前的, 先行的

examples.en: What do you know about the antecedents of the war?
Alchemy was the antecedent of chemistry.
If we alter the construction of such sentences, the missing antecedent is often restored.

anterior.definition: a. of or near the head end or toward the front plane of a body\ns. earlier in time
anterior.translation: a. 前面的, 先前的\n[医] 前的

examples.en: The head, expanding from the neck, contracts to a bluntly pointed anterior end.
The sounds babies make when they babble seem to contain a lot of anterior consonants.

anthem.definition: n. a song of devotion or loyalty (as to a nation or school)

examples.en: The text of the national anthem of Canada was first written in French.
examples.zh: 加拿大国歌的歌词最初是用法文写的。

examples.en: Estonia has its own national anthem.
examples.zh: 爱沙尼亚有它自己的国歌。

examples.en: Esperanto has its own anthem.
examples.zh: 世界语有自己的圣歌。

anthropology.definition: n. the social science that studies the origins and social relationships of human beings
anthropology.translation: n. 人类学\n[医] 人类学

examples.en: I'm an anthropology research student, and my topic is 'Chinese medicine in Britain'.
examples.zh: 我是人类学的研究学生，课题是“中医在英国”。

antibiotic.definition: n. a chemical substance derivable from a mold or bacterium that can kill microorganisms and cure bacterial infections\na. of or relating to antibiotic drugs
antibiotic.translation: n. 抗生素\na. 抗生的

examples.en: We've got eyedrops and an oral antibiotic to give them.
Keep taking this antibiotic until it is gone.
He managed to get her antibiotics that saved her life.

antique.definition:
n. any piece of furniture or decorative object or the like produced in a former period and valuable because of its beauty or rarity
v. shop for antiques
v. give an antique appearance to
s. made in or typical of earlier times and valued for its age
antique.translation: n. 古董, 古物\na. 古老的, 古风的, 旧式的, 过时的

examples.en: He came across this old coin in an antique shop.
examples.zh: 他偶然在古董店里发现了这个旧硬币。

examples.en: Can you tell me where the nearest antique shop is?
examples.zh: 你能告诉我最近的古玩店在哪里吗？

examples.en: She has a great love for antique goods.
examples.zh: 她对古董很感兴趣。

antiquity.definition: n. the historic period preceding the Middle Ages in Europe\nn. an artifact surviving from the past
antiquity.translation: n. 古老, 古代, 古代人, 古物

examples.en: The lighthouse of Alexandria was the tallest lighthouse in Antiquity.
The terms "Jew," "Hebrew," and "Israelite" were already interchangeable in antiquity.
Since antiquity, man has always wanted to fly.

ape.definition: n. any of various primates with short tails or no tail at all\nv. imitate uncritically and in every aspect
ape.translation: n. 无尾猿\n[计] 应用程序评价

examples.en: Ziri told Walid to stop walking around like an ape.
Tom is a human, an ape, and a mammal.
The missing link between ape and man is us.

apparel.translation: n. 衣服, 外表\nvt. 使穿衣, 装饰

examples.en: We went up two floors to reach the apparel stalls.
We went up by two floors to reach the apparel stalls.
Warm and comfortable apparel is necessary for winter outings.

appendix.definition: n. supplementary material that is collected and appended at the back of a book\nn. a vestigial process that extends from the lower end of the cecum and that resembles a small pouch
appendix.translation: n. 附录, 附加物, 阑尾\n[化] 增补

examples.en: Why the heck do humans have an appendix in the first place?
I am going to remove the appendix.
Tom had to have his appendix removed.

applause.definition: n. a demonstration of approval by clapping the hands together
applause.translation: n. 鼓掌, 喝彩, 赞许

examples.en: The king’s portrait was unveiled to great applause.
examples.zh: 国王的肖像揭晓，收获了热烈的掌声。

examples.en: His speech won the immediate applause of the audience.
examples.zh: 他的演说赢得了观众热烈的掌声。

examples.en: The portrait of the king was unveiled and received enthusiastic applause.
examples.zh: 国王的肖像揭晓，收获了热烈的掌声。

apprentice.definition: n. works for an expert to learn a trade\nv. be or work as an apprentice
apprentice.translation: n. 学徒, 生手\nvt. 使做学徒

examples.en: He's your senior fellow apprentice.
examples.zh: 他是你的师兄。

aquatic.definition: n. a plant that lives in or on water\na. relating to or consisting of or being in water\na. operating or living or growing in water
aquatic.translation: n. 水生动物, 水生植物\na. 水生的, 水中的, 水上的

examples.en: Ducks feed on worms, crustaceans, aquatic insects, and algae.
The lotus is an aquatic plant with very large leaves and flowers.
Runoff from upstream development had almost destroyed all aquatic life in the stream.

arable.definition: s. (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
arable.translation: a. 适于耕种的, 可耕的

examples.en: Arable land is land that can be used to grow crops.
American companies owned almost all of Cuba's arable lands.
Algeria's arable lands are concentrated in the north of the country.

arc.definition: n. a continuous portion of a circle
arc.translation: n. 弧, 弧形, 弓形, 弧光\n[化] 弧

examples.en: Most arc lamps can only be found in museums nowadays.
The Arc of Triumph was built to greet Napoleon's army.
Carbon arc lamps emit a spectrum similar to sunlight.

archaeology.definition: n the branch of anthropology that studies prehistoric people and their cultures

examples.en: In archaeology, it is important to keep findings intact and undamaged.
Archaeology is critical to the study of all history, but especially prehistory.
Mary is a student of archaeology.

ardent.definition: s. characterized by intense emotion\ns. characterized by strong enthusiasm\ns. glowing or shining like fire
ardent.translation: a. 热心的, 激动的, 燃烧般的\n[医] 灼热的; 热心的

examples.en: This pair of lovers were carrying on an ardent correspondence.
It is our ardent hope that the war will end soon.
Mastering science is an ardent wish of our youth.

arid.definition: s. lacking sufficient water or rainfall\ns. lacking vitality or spirit; lifeless
arid.translation: a. 干燥的, 不毛的

examples.en: It is an arid region, almost a desert.
examples.zh: 这是片干燥地区，几乎是一片荒漠。

armor.definition: n. protective covering made of metal and used in combat\nn. a military unit consisting of armored fighting vehicles\nn. tough more-or-less rigid protective covering of an animal or plant
armor.translation: n. 盔甲, 潜水服, 装甲\nvt. 为...装甲

examples.en: The female armor in this video game is so skimpy.
The bronze armor was useless against the Saxons' relentless attack.
He who wears armor falls with a big crash!

aroma.definition: n. a distinctive odor that is pleasant
aroma.translation: n. 浓香, 香气\n[医] 香气, 芳香气

examples.en: The room hasn't been cleaned recently, so it now has a foul aroma.
examples.zh: 这个房间最近都没打扫过，有一股臭味。

artillery.definition: n. large but transportable armament\nn. an army unit that uses big guns
artillery.translation: n. 火炮, 炮兵, 炮术\n[机] 火炮, 炮兵

examples.en: The US carried out highly destructive artillery strikes in Iraq.
A volley of artillery fire completely destroyed the buildings.
Tactical nuclear weapons can be fired from artillery.

ascribe.translation: vt. 归因于, 归咎于\n[法] 归咎于

examples.en: He ascribes his failure to bad luck.
examples.zh: 他把他的错误归咎于坏运气。

assassinate.definition: v. murder; especially of socially prominent persons\nv. destroy or damage seriously, as of someone's reputation
assassinate.translation: vt. 暗杀, 行刺\n[法] 暗杀, 行刺, 中伤

examples.en: They attempted to assassinate the president.
examples.zh: 他们企图暗杀总统。

assimilate.definition:
v. become similar to one's environment
v. make similar
v. take (gas, light or heat) into a solution
v. become similar in sound
assimilate.translation: vt. 使同化, 吸收, 使相拟, 把...比作\nvi. 被吸收, 被同化

examples.en: The weak easily assimilate the opinions of the strong.
It can be difficult for newcomers to a country to assimilate.
The US government attempted to assimilate Native American children.

asteroid.definition: n. any of numerous small celestial bodies composed of rock and metal that move around the sun (mainly between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter)\ns. shaped like a star
asteroid.translation: n. 小行星, 海盘车\na. 星状的

examples.en: The asteroid broke up into small pieces as it entered Earth's atmosphere.
examples.zh: 进入地球大气层后，小行星分裂成了无数的小块。

examples.en: Don't mix up comets and asteroids.
examples.zh: 不要把流星和小行星搞混了。

examples.en: The space probe Lucy is expected to arrive in 2025 to the proximity of the asteroid Donaldjohanson.
examples.zh: 太空探测器露西预计将于 2025 年抵达小行星唐纳德约翰逊附近。

asylum.definition: n a shelter from danger or hardship\nn a hospital for mentally incompetent or unbalanced person
asylum.translation: n. 庇护, 收容所\n[医] 养育院

examples.en: On the 20th of January 2025, the inmates took over the asylum.
examples.zh: 2025 年 1 月 20 日，精神病患接管了精神病院。

examples.en: This world is just an insane asylum.
examples.zh: 世界就是一个疯子的囚笼。

attest.definition: v. provide evidence for; stand as proof of; show by one's behavior, attitude, or external attributes\nv. authenticate, affirm to be true, genuine, or correct, as in an official capacity\nv. establish or verify the usage of
attest.translation: vi. 证明, 表明, 作证\nvt. 为...作证

examples.en: I will attest that I did not hear that.
The fingerprints on the knife attest to her guilt.
I can attest to everything she just said.

attic.definition:
n. the dialect of Ancient Greek spoken and written in Attica and Athens and Ionia
n. informal terms for a human head
n. (architecture) a low wall at the top of the entablature; hides the roof
a. of or relating to Attica or its inhabitants or to the dialect spoken in Athens in classical times
attic.translation: n. 阁楼, 顶楼\n[医] 鼓室上隐窝

examples.en: They cleaned everything, from the basement to the attic.
examples.zh: 他们从地下室到阁楼都打扫了。

examples.en: What were you doing in the attic?
examples.zh: 你在阁楼上做了什么？

examples.en: Tom's kids were in the attic.
examples.zh: 汤姆孩子们在阁楼。

attire.definition: n. clothing of a distinctive style or for a particular occasion
attire.translation: n. 服装, 盛装\nvt. 使穿衣, 打扮

examples.en: A T-shirt is not appropriate attire for a job interview.
A T-shirt isn't appropriate attire for a job interview.
What kind of women's attire does Tom like?

auditorium.definition: n. the area of a theater or concert hall where the audience sits
auditorium.translation: n. 听众席, 礼堂\n[医] 大讲堂, 大会堂

examples.en: I knew it would be hot in the auditorium.
examples.zh: 我就知道礼堂里会很热。

augment.definition: v. enlarge or increase\nv. grow or intensify
augment.translation: v. 增加, 增长\n[计] 增加; 增量; 添加

examples.en: Peasants often have a secondary activity to augment their income.
Jugurtha sought to augment his power.
Prem Buth repairs bikes and motorbikes from his house to augment his income from farming.

auspicious.definition: a. auguring favorable circumstances and good luck
auspicious.translation: a. 吉兆的, 幸运的

examples.en: It's an auspicious time to launch a new organization.
His own debut would be far less auspicious.
Today is an auspicious day.

austere.definition: s. severely simple\ns. of a stern or strict bearing or demeanor; forbidding in aspect
austere.translation: a. 严峻的, 禁欲的, 简朴的

examples.en: Ms. Eichler had a notorious reputation for being austere to her students.
examples.zh: 艾希勒女士对学生严厉是出了名的。

autonomy.definition: n. immunity from arbitrary exercise of authority: political independence\nn. personal independence
autonomy.translation: n. 自治, 自治权\n[医] 自主性

examples.en: People would have more autonomy if they had a job.
Local governments in Algeria should be given greater fiscal autonomy.
The Polisario Front has rejected Morocco's plan for "autonomy."

avalanche.definition: n. a slide of large masses of snow and ice and mud down a mountain\nn. a sudden appearance of an overwhelming number of things\nv. gather into a huge mass and roll down a mountain, of snow
avalanche.translation: n. 雪崩, 山崩, 大量\nvi. 崩塌\nvt. 大量涌至

examples.en: Nobody knows just how many people died in the avalanche.
The rescuers pulled out the young girl from the avalanche.
How long can you survive buried in an avalanche?

avert.translation: vt. 转开, 避免, 防止

examples.en: Mary quickly averted her eyes.
examples.zh: 玛丽赶紧避开了眼光。

avid.definition: s. (often followed by `for') ardently or excessively desirous\ns. marked by active interest and enthusiasm
avid.translation: a. 渴望的, 急切的, 劲头十足的

examples.en: That is why I am not an avid bike rider.
He's an avid reader with a vast knowledge of literature.
Yanni has been an avid cyclist all his life.

accountancy.definition: n. the occupation of maintaining and auditing records and preparing financial reports for a business
accountancy.translation: n. 会计工作, 会计学\n[经] 会计工作, 会计学术, 会计职业

examples.en: It's possible to branch out from computing to jobs in banking, accountancy and so on.
examples.zh: 有可能将电脑工作扩展到银行业务, 会计业务等等。

acquit.definition: v. pronounce not guilty of criminal charges
acquit.translation: vt. 无罪释放, 表现, 使履行\n[法] 开释, 释放, 免

examples.en: The court acquitted him of the charge of murder.
examples.zh: 法庭对他的谋杀罪名作出了无罪判决。

examples.en: It doesn’t matter what you say, he’ll be acquitted because of depression.
examples.zh: 因为他有忧郁症，所以不管你说什么他都会被无罪释放。

alias.definition: n. a name that has been assumed temporarily\nr. as known or named at another time or place
alias.translation: n. 别名, 化名\nadv. 以化名为人所知\n[计] 别名; 替换入口

examples.en: I escaped to Australia under the alias of Tom Jackson.
My alias has no relation to my real name.
Tom uses an alias when he plays video games.

align.definition:
v. place in a line or arrange so as to be parallel or straight
v. be or come into adjustment with
v. align oneself with a group or a way of thinking
v. bring (components or parts) into proper or desirable coordination correlation
align.translation: vi. 排列, 排成一行, 结盟\nvt. 使结盟, 使成一行, 校正

examples.en: You must align the faucet spout with the sink drain.
Align your step with the lion's, you will know serenity.
We can use braces to align your teeth better.

allegiance.definition: n. the loyalty that citizens owe to their country (or subjects to their sovereign)

examples.en: The knight swore an oath of allegiance to the king.
examples.zh: 骑士宣誓效忠于国王。

examples.en: The knight swears an oath of allegiance to the King.
examples.zh: 骑士宣誓效忠于国王。

examples.en: I pledge allegiance to the flag.
examples.zh: 我向国旗宣誓效忠。

alumni.definition: n a person who has received a degree from a school (high school or college or university)
alumni.translation: pl. 男毕业生, 男校友

examples.en: The event was open to students and alumni.
Alumni are listed by their department of study.
The cruise for M.I.T. alumni was called "A Ship of Tools."

ammunition.definition: n. projectiles to be fired from a gun\nn. any nuclear or chemical or biological material that can be used as a weapon of mass destruction\nn. information that can be used to attack or defend a claim or argument or viewpoint
ammunition.translation: n. 军火, 弹药\n[机] 弹药

examples.en: Yanni was arrested with four hundred rounds of ammunition.
Layla had a lot more ammunition than Sami.
How did live ammunition get on set, anyway?

aquarium.definition: n. a tank or pool or bowl filled with water for keeping live fish and underwater animals
aquarium.translation: n. 水族馆, 养鱼池, 水草缸\n[医] 培养缸

examples.en: I needed to add water to my aquarium.
examples.zh: 我需要往我的鱼缸里加水。

archipelago.definition: n. a group of many islands in a large body of water
archipelago.translation: n. 群岛, 多岛屿的海

examples.en: The Japanese archipelago is struck by a terrible heat wave.
The Virgin Islands are an archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean.
Hawaii is a volcanic archipelago in the Pacific Ocean.

archive.definition: n. a depository containing historical records and documents\nv. put into an archive
archive.translation: vt. 把...存档\nn. 档案馆, 档案文件\n[计] 挡案库, 存档

examples.en: I created an archive of my emails.
examples.zh: 我给自己的邮件做了一份档案。

examples.en: I'm downloading this internet archive.
examples.zh: 我在下载这份网络档案。

artery.definition: n. a blood vessel that carries blood from the heart to the body\nn. a major thoroughfare that bears important traffic
artery.translation: n. 动脉, 干道, 要道\n[医] 动脉

examples.en: The patient injured his upper cervical posterior spinal artery by sneezing.
The Nile is the vital artery of Egypt.
I've got a bad heart: coronary artery disease.

astound.translation: vt. 使惊骇, 使大惊

examples.en: Foreigners astound me.
examples.zh: 外国人使我惊讶。

abbey.definition: n. a church associated with a monastery or convent\nn. a convent ruled by an abbess\nn. a monastery ruled by an abbot

examples.en: I want to see the medieval tiles in the nearby abbey.
Many music-lovers make pilgrimages to places like Abbey Road in London.
We walked through the ruins of the abbey.

abdomen.definition: n. the region of the body of a vertebrate between the thorax and the pelvis

examples.en: Most of an insect's organs are inside its abdomen.
Ziri ran his finger down Rima's chest and abdomen.
The liver is in the upper right quadrant of the abdomen.

abscess.definition: n. symptom consisting of a localized collection of pus surrounded by inflamed tissue
abscess.translation: n. 脓肿\nvi. 形成脓肿

examples.en: He has an abscess on his foot.
She has an abscess on her foot.
He had an abscess on his tonsil.

adobe.definition: n. the clay from which adobe bricks are made\nn. sun-dried brick; used in hot dry climates
adobe.translation: n. 风干土坯\n[化] 风干砖; 土砖; 灰质粘土; 多孔粘土

examples.en: Some Southwestern Native Americans lived in adobe houses called pueblos.
At last! Adobe dumps this shitty Flash for mobiles.
Adobe and Apple both have top-notch video editing programs.

aerospace.definition: n. the atmosphere and outer space considered as a whole
aerospace.translation: n. 航天空间, 航天技术

examples.en: His dream is to become an aerospace engineer.
examples.zh: 他的梦想是成为航天航空工程师。

airborne.definition: s. moved or conveyed by or through air
airborne.translation: a. 升空的, 空运的, 空中传播的, 空降的

examples.en: Once we are airborne, you make unbuckle your seatbelts.
Gnarly! You were airborne for like 10 seconds.
Be careful, this virus is airborne.

akin.definition: s. similar in quality or character\ns. related by blood
akin.translation: a. 同类的, 同族的, 同源的

examples.en: Akin to someone driving a donkey up an incline.
This problem is akin to the one we had last year.
The process of artistic creation isn't necessarily akin to factory production.

algebra.definition: n. the mathematics of generalized arithmetical operations

examples.en: Many pupils are poor at algebra.
examples.zh: 很多小学生学不好代数。

examples.en: Algebra is my favorite subject.
examples.zh: 代数是我最喜欢的科目。

alphabetical.definition: a relating to or expressed by a writing system that uses an alphabet\na arranged in order according to the alphabet
alphabetical.translation: a. 依字母顺序的, 字母的

examples.en: Could you rearrange this list so it's in alphabetical order?
examples.zh: 你能把这清单按字母顺序排列吗？

examples.en: The list was in alphabetical order.
examples.zh: 清单依字母顺序排序。

ambiguity.definition: n. an expression whose meaning cannot be determined from its context\nn. unclearness by virtue of having more than one meaning
ambiguity.translation: n. 不明确, 含糊\n[计] 二义性; 多义性

examples.en: The law is full of ambiguities.
examples.zh: 法律有很多不明确的地方。

ammonia.definition: n. a pungent gas compounded of nitrogen and hydrogen (NH3)
ammonia.translation: n. 氨水, 阿摩尼亚\n[化] 氨

examples.en: Don't mix ammonia and bleach together.
examples.zh: 别把氨水和漂白剂混在一起。

amphibian.definition: n. a flat-bottomed motor vehicle that can travel on land or water\nn. an airplane designed to take off and land on water\nn. cold-blooded vertebrate typically living on land but breeding in water; aquatic larvae undergo metamorphosis into adult form
amphibian.translation: a. 两栖类的, 水陆两用的\nn. 两栖动物, 水旱两生植物, 水陆两用飞机

examples.en: Fish, amphibians, and reptiles are cold-blooded animals.
examples.zh: 鱼类、两栖类和爬行类都是冷血动物。

analytic.definition: a. using or subjected to a methodology using algebra and calculus\na. using or skilled in using analysis (i.e., separating a whole--intellectual or substantial--into its elemental parts or basic principles)\na. expressing a grammatical category by using two or more words rather than inflection
analytic.translation: a. 分析的, 善于分析的, 解析的\n[医] 分析的

examples.en: This is an analytic language.
Filtered back projection is an analytic reconstruction algorithm designed to overcome the limitations of conventional back projection.

android.definition: n. an automaton that resembles a human being
android.translation: n. 机器人\n[医] 男性样的

examples.en: Leon’s android can do whatever he wants.
examples.zh: 里昂的机器人可以做任何他想要完成的事。

examples.en: I'm developing an Android application.
examples.zh: 我正在开发一个安卓应用。

examples.en: I've started Android programming.
examples.zh: 我已经开始了我的安卓编程之旅。

animated.definition: a. having life or vigor or spirit\ns. made to appear to move as living creatures do
animated.translation: a. 活生生的, 能活动的, 活泼的, 欢快的

examples.en: "My new animated movie is called 'Stretchie: End of Clays Part II,'" said Tom.
examples.zh: 汤姆说：「我推出的全新动画电影叫做《伸展世界：黏土的末日 (下)》。」

anonymity.definition: n. the state of being anonymous
anonymity.translation: n. 匿名, 姓氏不明\n[计] 匿名信件

examples.en: Anonymity or detailed reference are both fine.
examples.zh: 不留名或详细的参考什么都可以。

examples.en: When using this information, I will follow any conditions you specify, whether that's anonymity or giving detailed reference.
examples.zh: 在使用这份问卷的信息时，我会遵照您提出的条件，不留您的姓名或者关于您的任何详细信息。

ant.definition: n. social insect living in organized colonies; characteristically the males and fertile queen have wings during breeding season; wingless sterile females are the workers

examples.en: The area around the melting ice cream was crawling with ants.
examples.zh: 在那滩冰淇淋的周围，有一群蚂蚁在爬来爬去。

examples.en: The lonely man derives pleasure from observing ants.
examples.zh: 那个孤僻的人以观察蚂蚁取乐。

examples.en: There's a row of ants coming in and out of the kitchen.
examples.zh: 有一排蚂蚁在厨房里进进出出。

antenna.definition: n. an electrical device that sends or receives radio or television signals\nn. sensitivity similar to that of a receptor organ\nn. one of a pair of mobile appendages on the head of e.g. insects and crustaceans; typically sensitive to touch and taste
antenna.translation: n. 天线, 触须, 触角\n[化] 天线

examples.en: The man tried to install his own antenna.
examples.zh: 这男人试着安装他自己的天线。

antidote.definition: n. a remedy that stops or controls the effects of a poison
antidote.translation: n. 解毒剂, 解毒药\n[化] 解毒药

examples.en: There is no antidote for the venom of this snake.
Laughing is the most effective antidote to bad temper.
You are truly an antidote for my melancholy.

apex.definition: n. the point on the celestial sphere toward which the sun and solar system appear to be moving relative to the fixed stars
apex.translation: n. 顶, 尖端, 最高潮\n[医] 尖, 尖端

examples.en: The polar bear is the apex predator of the Arctic.
Polar bears are the apex predators of the Arctic.
In Tasmania, thylacines were the only marsupial apex predators.

arcade.definition: n. a covered passageway with shops and stalls on either side\nn. a structure composed of a series of arches supported by columns
arcade.translation: n. 拱廊, 拱形建筑物, 有拱廊的街道\n[医] 弓形组织, 连拱

examples.en: I have a lot of arcade machines.
examples.zh: 我有很多电玩。

examples.en: Real-time strategy games usually include arcade elements.
examples.zh: 即时策略游戏通常会融入街机元素。

armpit.definition: n. the hollow under the arm where it is joined to the shoulder
armpit.translation: n. 腋窝\n[医] 腋, 腋窝

examples.en: She could feel a small lump in her armpit.
She lives in the armpit of the world.
Then don't put your nose in my armpit.

arson.definition: n. malicious burning to destroy property
arson.translation: n. 纵火, 纵火罪\n[法] 纵火, 放火

examples.en: The fire that broke out last night was judged to be caused by arson.
examples.zh: 昨晚的火灾被断定为由纵火引起的。

asbestos.definition: n. a fibrous amphibole; used for making fireproof articles; inhaling fibers can cause asbestosis or lung cancer

examples.en: Asbestos are linked to a number of deadly lung diseases.
Tom has been exposed to asbestos on the job.
In Spain asbestos is a huge problem that is kept secret.

aspirin.definition: n. the acetylated derivative of salicylic acid; used as an analgesic anti-inflammatory drug (trade names Bayer, Empirin, and St. Joseph) usually taken in tablet form; used as an antipyretic; slows clotting of the blood by poisoning platelets
aspirin.translation: n. 阿斯匹林\n[化] 乙酰水杨酸; 阿司匹灵; 邻乙酸基苯甲酸

examples.en: My head hurts. Maybe I should take an aspirin.
examples.zh: 我头痛。可能我该吃阿司匹林。

examples.en: I would like to buy some aspirin.
examples.zh: 我想买点阿司匹林。

examples.en: I'd like a packet of aspirin.
examples.zh: 我要一盒阿司匹林。

asterisk.definition: n. a star-shaped character * used in printing
asterisk.translation: n. 星号\n[计] 星号, 星号通配符

examples.en: What's the meaning of an asterisk in a regular expression?
They don't know how to use an asterisk.
The footnotes are marked with an asterisk.

astronomer.definition: n. a physicist who studies astronomy

examples.en: Astronomers have discovered a galaxy that has almost no dark matter.
examples.zh: 天文学家们发现了一个几乎没有暗物质的星系。

atlas.definition:
n. (Greek mythology) a Titan who was forced by Zeus to bear the sky on his shoulders
n. a collection of maps in book form
n. the 1st cervical vertebra
n. a figure of a man used as a supporting column
atlas.translation: n. 地图集, 图表集\n[计] 自动测试和负载分析系统

examples.en: Fyodor was on a camping trail in the Blida Atlas.
Felix went on a trip to the Blida Atlas Mountains.
We took a field trip to the Blida Atlas Mountains.

aurora.definition: n. an atmospheric phenomenon consisting of bands of light caused by charged solar particles following the earth's magnetic lines of force\nn. (Roman mythology) goddess of the dawn; counterpart of Greek Eos
aurora.translation: n. 曙光, 极光, 奥罗拉(曙光女神)\n[电] 极光

examples.en: The aurora is a phenomenon characteristic of the polar regions.
examples.zh: 极光是极地特有的自然现象。

auto.definition: n a motor vehicle with four wheels; usually propelled by an internal combustion engine
auto.translation: n. 汽车\npref. 表示"自己"、"本身", 表示"自己的", 表示"自动的"

examples.en: Yanni bought this kit at a local auto parts store.
The building you see over there is an auto factory.
Auto imports will take a nose-dive in the first quarter.

algorithm.definition: n. a precise rule (or set of rules) specifying how to solve some problem

examples.en: The use of trust-region algorithms is becoming more and more frequent.
examples.zh: 信赖域的算法越来越常用。

examples.en: Data compression algorithms can be classified in two categories: those with data loss and those without data loss.
examples.zh: 压缩数据的算法能分为两种：一种会造成数据损失，另一种则不会。

examples.en: He devoted the last years of his life to writing his autobiography.
examples.zh: 他晚年致力于写自传。

apron.definition: n. a garment of cloth or leather or plastic that is tied about the waist and worn to protect your clothing\nn. (golf) the part of the fairway leading onto the green\nn. a paved surface where aircraft stand while not being used

examples.en: Mother is in the kitchen wearing an apron.
examples.zh: 妈妈在厨房里围着围裙。

examples.en: My mother has a red apron.
examples.zh: 我妈有一条红色的围裙。

examples.en: Tom put on an apron.
examples.zh: 汤姆穿上了一条围裙。

admiral.definition: n. the supreme commander of a fleet; ranks above a vice admiral and below a fleet admiral\nn. any of several brightly colored butterflies
admiral.translation: n. 舰队司令, 海军上将, 旗舰

examples.en: There is a statue of Admiral Nelson in Trafalgar Square.
The commander of the admiral's fleet was Admiral Nagumo.
Admiral, an unidentified vessel is approaching our position.

acupuncture.definition: n. treatment of pain or disease by inserting the tips of needles at specific points on the skin
acupuncture.translation: n. 针刺, 针刺疗法\nvt. 施以针灸

examples.en: Many people believe that acupuncture can cure diseases.
examples.zh: 很多人都相信针灸有治愈疾病的功效。

examples.en: Many people believe acupuncture can cure diseases.
examples.zh: 很多人都相信针灸有治愈疾病的功效。

anchovy.definition: n. tiny fishes usually canned or salted; used for hors d'oeuvres or as seasoning in sauces\nn. small herring-like plankton-eating fishes often canned whole or as paste; abundant in tropical waters worldwide

examples.en: "What toppings do you want on the pizza?" "Anything but anchovies."
When was the last time you ate anchovies?
Can I have some anchovies with olives?

apricot.definition: n. Asian tree having clusters of usually white blossoms and edible fruit resembling the peach\nn. downy yellow to rosy-colored fruit resembling a small peach
apricot.translation: n. 杏子, 杏树, 杏黄色\na. 杏黄色的

examples.en: The more you eat Kuqa's apricots, the more of them you'll want to eat.
examples.zh: 库车的杏子你越吃越想吃。

artichoke.definition: n. Mediterranean thistlelike plant widely cultivated for its large edible flower head\nn. a thistlelike flower head with edible fleshy leaves and heart
artichoke.translation: n. 朝鲜蓟\n[医] 朝鲜蓟

examples.en: Tom says that he has never eaten an artichoke.
After they've been blanched, the artichokes can be frozen.
At the market we bought peaches, artichokes, courgettes, strawberries and aubergines.

avocado.definition: n. a pear-shaped tropical fruit with green or blackish skin and rich yellowish pulp enclosing a single large seed\nn. tropical American tree bearing large pulpy green fruits\ns. of the dull yellowish green of the meat of an avocado

examples.en: I enjoy a veggie burger with avocado.
examples.zh: 我喜欢吃加酪梨的素食汉堡。

examples.en: Does anyone know a good method of eating avocados that will bring out their taste?
examples.zh: 有谁知道怎么吃酪梨才能更好地凸显它的味道？

examples.en: I ate five avocados.
examples.zh: 我吃了五个牛油果。

alligator.definition: n. leather made from alligator's hide\nn. either of two amphibious reptiles related to crocodiles but with shorter broader snouts\nv. crack and acquire the appearance of alligator hide, as from weathering or improper application; of paint and varnishes
alligator.translation: n. 短吻鳄\n[机] 两栖装甲车

examples.en: What to do if you're attacked by an alligator?
An alligator has been caught on tape eating a small shark.
What's the difference between a crocodile and an alligator?

accordion.definition: n. a portable box-shaped free-reed instrument; the reeds are made to vibrate by air from the bellows controlled by the player
accordion.translation: n. 手风琴\na. 可折叠的

examples.en: I forgot that Tom knew how to play the accordion.
A white-haired man was playing an accordion outside the shop.
A white-haired man was playing an accordion outside the store.

accustom.definition: v make psychologically or physically used (to something)

examples.en: You have to accustom yourself to the crowded trains in Tokyo.
examples.zh: 你要习惯东京拥挤的火车。

analyze.definition: v. consider in detail and subject to an analysis in order to discover essential features or meaning\nv. make a mathematical, chemical, or grammatical analysis of; break down into components or essential features\nv. break down into components or essential features
analyze.translation: vt. 分析, 细察, 分解\n[机] 分析

examples.en: We want to analyze your urine.
examples.zh: 我们想验一下您的尿液。

examples.en: The aviation expert analyzed the statistics in detail.
examples.zh: 航空专家详细分析了统计数据。

examples.en: We've had it analyzed.
examples.zh: 我们已经将它做了分析。

articulate.definition: v. unite by forming a joint or joints\nv. express or state clearly\na. expressing yourself easily or characterized by clear expressive language
articulate.translation: a. 发音清晰的, 口才好的\nvt. 明白地说, 以关节连接, 使成为系统的整体

examples.en: Sometimes he has difficulty being articulate about his views.
examples.zh: 他有时候会难以清楚地表达他的意见。

aspiration.definition: n. a will to succeed\nn. a manner of articulation involving an audible release of breath
aspiration.translation: n. 热望, 志向, 渴望\n[医] 吸入; 吸[引], 吸引术

examples.en: Each has their aspiration.
examples.zh: 人各有志。

athletic.definition: a. relating to or befitting athletics or athletes\ns. having a sturdy and well proportioned body

examples.en: The boy put on his athletic shoes and ran outside.
examples.zh: 那个男孩穿上了他的运动鞋，跑向外面。

examples.en: Owing to the rain, the athletic meeting was put off.
examples.zh: 运动会因为下雨延后了。

examples.en: Jane had her hair cut short before the athletic meet.
examples.zh: Jane在运动会之前把头发剃短了。

atomic.definition: a. of or relating to or comprising atoms\ns. immeasurably small
atomic.translation: a. 原子的, 原子能的\n[医] 原子的

examples.en: The atomic bomb is the offspring of 20th century physics.
examples.zh: 原子弹是二十世纪物理学的产物。

examples.en: John Dalton was the creator of the atomic theory.
examples.zh: 约翰·道尔顿是原子学说的创始人

examples.en: The atomic reactor generates enormous amounts of thermal energy.
examples.zh: 原子反应堆发出大量的热能。

await.definition: v look forward to the probable occurrence of

examples.en: No one knew what awaited us.
examples.zh: 没人知道等待我们的是什么。

examples.en: Nobody knew what awaited us.
examples.zh: 没人知道等待我们的是什么。

examples.en: What punishment awaits him?
examples.zh: 他将面临什么样的惩罚？

awe.definition: n. an overwhelming feeling of wonder or admiration\nv. inspire awe in

examples.en: I am immediately in awe of you!
examples.zh: 我瞬间对你肃然起敬！

abort.definition:
n. the act of terminating a project or procedure before it is completed
v. terminate before completion
v. cease development, die, and be aborted
v. terminate a pregnancy by undergoing an abortion
abort.translation: vi. 流产, 中途失败\nvt. 使流产, 使失败, 使中止

examples.en: I don't want to abort the mission now.
"Yanni is coming." "Abort mission! Abort mission!"
Tom is in favor of aborting the mission.

abreast.definition: s. being up to particular standard or level especially in being up to date in knowledge\nr. alongside each other, facing in the same direction
abreast.translation: adv. 并肩地, 并列地

examples.en: These two are standing abreast.
examples.zh: 两人并肩站在一起。

absorption.definition: n. (chemistry) a process in which one substance permeates another; a fluid permeates or is dissolved by a liquid or solid\nn. (physics) the process in which incident radiated energy is retained without reflection or transmission on passing through a medium
absorption.translation: n. 吸收, 专心, 全神贯注\n[化] 吸收; 吸收作用

examples.en: Could you explain to me how food absorption takes place?
Would you like shoe inserts for shock absorption?
Could you explain how food absorption takes place?

academician.definition: n. someone elected to honorary membership in an academy\nn. a scholar who is skilled in academic disputation\nn. an educator who works at a college or university
academician.translation: n. 学会会员, 院士, 学究, 大学生, 学者

examples.en: Though brilliant, the academician was notorious for his lack of practical sense.
The academician spent years studying a single obscure poet from the 14th century.
As an academician, she valued precision.

accountability.definition: n. responsibility to someone or for some activity
accountability.translation: n. 负有责任, 可说明性\n[化] 衡算计量

examples.en: I take accountability for my mistake.
examples.zh: 我来承担失败的责任。

accounting.definition: n. a convincing explanation that reveals basic causes\nn. a system that provides quantitative information about finances\nn. a bookkeeper's chronological list of related debits and credits of a business; forms part of a ledger of accounts
accounting.translation: n. 会计学, 帐单, 清帐\n[计] 帐户处理, 记帐

examples.en: Do you know accounting?
examples.zh: 你懂会计吗？

ace.definition:
n. one of four playing cards in a deck having a single pip on its face
n. someone who is dazzlingly skilled in any field
n. a serve that the receiver is unable to reach
v. score an ace against
ace.translation: n. 幺点, 好手, 少许, 发球得分\na. 一流的, 杰出的\n[计] 应答允许, 自适应计算机试验, 自动呼叫设备, 自动执行控制

examples.en: She was within an ace of saying "I don't know".
examples.zh: 她差点要说「我不知道」了。

acting.definition: n. the performance of a part or role in a drama\ns. serving temporarily especially as a substitute
acting.translation: n. 演戏, 装腔作势\na. 代理的, 演出用的, 起作用的

examples.en: Her acting is on the level of a professional.
examples.zh: 她的演技堪比专业人士。

examples.en: "Has Cookie been acting weird lately?" "He's a cat."
examples.zh: 「曲奇最近行为怪异吗？」「他是一只猫。」

examples.en: Tom is acting as if nothing has happened.
examples.zh: 汤姆像什么也没发生一样行动。

addiction.definition: n. being abnormally tolerant to and dependent on something that is psychologically or physically habit-forming (especially alcohol or narcotic drugs)\nn. an abnormally strong craving\nn. (Roman law) a formal award by a magistrate of a thing or person to another person (as the award of a debtor to his creditor); a surrender to a master
addiction.translation: n. 入迷, 瘾\n[医] 瘾, 癖嗜

examples.en: There really is such a thing as Internet addiction.
examples.zh: 确实有网瘾这回事。

examples.en: People “diagnosed” with “Internet addiction” are nearly always diagnosed with other difficulties as well.
examples.zh: 诊断患有“网络成瘾症”的人差不多总是也有其他的困难。

examples.en: The concept of “Internet addiction” implies that “the Internet” is some sort of definable activity.
examples.zh: “网络成瘾症”这个理念将意味着“网络”是一种可以下定义的活动。

adequacy.definition: n. the quality of being able to meet a need satisfactorily: "he questioned the adequacy of the usual sentimental interpretation of the Golden Rule"

examples.en: Tom behaves obligingly to prove his adequacy.
While this accord represents a breakthrough after months of negotiations, that says nothing about its adequacy.

administrate.definition: v work in an administrative capacity; supervise or be in charge of

examples.en: When Spain colonized the Philippines, they were administrated by Mexico City. So it was Mexican Spanish, not Castilian Spanish, that influenced Tagalog.
examples.zh: 当西班牙殖民了菲律宾时，是从墨西哥城管理它的。于是他加禄语是收到了墨西哥式西班牙语的影响，而不卡斯蒂利亚式的。

examples.en: Admittedly, it wasn't the best meal I've ever eaten.
examples.zh: 不可否认，那并不是我吃过最好的一顿饭。

adolescence.definition: n. the time period between the beginning of puberty and adulthood\nn. in the state that someone is in between puberty and adulthood
adolescence.translation: n. 青春期\n[医] 青年期, 青春期

examples.en: In adolescence, I hated life and was continually on the verge of suicide, from which, however, I was restrained by the desire to know more mathematics.
examples.zh: 在青春期，我厌倦生活，并持续陷入自杀的边缘。然而，在那期间，对数学知识的渴望，使我抑制住了那些负面情绪。

adoption.definition: n. the act of accepting with approval; favorable reception\nn. a legal proceeding that creates a parent-child relation between persons not related by blood; the adopted child is entitled to all privileges belonging to a natural child of the adoptive parents (including the right to inherit)
adoption.translation: n. 采用, 采纳, 收养\n[法] 收养, 采纳, 采用

examples.en: Igor paid fifty euros for the German Shepherd's adoption fee.
I think I'll put up my child for adoption.
How do you put a sentence up for adoption?

adorable.definition: s. lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
adorable.translation: a. 可崇拜的, 值得敬慕的, 可爱的

examples.en: He loves his puppy. His puppy is really adorable.
examples.zh: 他爱他的狗，那只小狗真的很可爱。

examples.en: How can there exist a creature as adorable as a cat?
examples.zh: 怎么会有猫咪这么可爱的生物？

examples.en: Ah Mei is an adorable girl.
examples.zh: 阿美是个可爱的女孩。

adore.translation: vt. 崇拜, 爱慕, 喜爱\nvi. 崇拜, 爱慕

examples.en: The students adore the new English teacher.
examples.zh: 学生们崇拜新的英语老师。

examples.en: She adores her older brother.
examples.zh: 她爱慕她哥哥。

adulthood.definition: n. the period of time in your life after your physical growth has stopped and you are fully developed\nn. the state (and responsibilities) of a person who has attained maturity
adulthood.translation: n. 成年\n[医] 成人期

examples.en: The graduation from elementary school to middle school is regarded by some as the first step towards adulthood.
examples.zh: 有些人认为从小学升到中学是踏入成年的第一步。

adventurer.definition: n. a person who enjoys taking risks
adventurer.translation: n. 冒险家, 投机者\n[法] 冒险者, 投机者

examples.en: Khaki shorts with cargo pockets do not make you an adventurer.
examples.zh: 单有卡其裤，还成不了冒险家。

advisory.definition: n. an announcement that usually advises or warns the public of some threat\ns. giving advice
advisory.translation: a. 顾问的, 咨询的, 劝告的\n[法] 劝告的, 忠告的, 咨询的

examples.en: The committee can only act in an advisory capacity.
There's a heat advisory in effect until Monday evening.
A wind advisory is in effect until the storm front passes.

advocacy.definition: n. active support of an idea or cause etc.; especially the act of pleading or arguing for something
advocacy.translation: n. 拥护, 支持, 鼓吹, 辩护, 辩护术\n[法] 辩护, 拥护, 提倡

examples.en: He volunteered at an advocacy group.
Advocacy was always his passion.
Health advocacy groups that have been warning of possible cell phone-cancer links are praising the WHO pronouncement.

affix.definition: n. a linguistic element added to a word to produce an inflected or derived form\nv. attach to\nv. attach or become attached to a stem word
affix.translation: vt. 使附于, 署名, 粘贴, 盖印于\nn. 附加物, 词缀

examples.en: Do not forget to affix the stamp to the envelope.
Please affix a passport-sized photograph to this form.
Did you forget to affix Form 6A?

affixation.definition: n. the result of adding an affix to a root word\nn. formation of a word by means of an affix

examples.en: Smith's approach differs greatly from others in that he did not take the affixation into consideration.

affluence.translation: n. 富裕, 丰富, 流注\n[医] 丰富, 流入

examples.en: Live in affluence.
examples.zh: 过富足的生活。

affordability.translation: n. 支付能力；负担能力；可购性

afloat.definition: a. borne on the water; floating\ns. covered with water
afloat.translation: a. 飘浮着的, 在海上的, 浸满水的, 在进行中的\nadv. 飘浮着, 在海上, 浸满水, 在进行中

examples.en: Yanni was working two jobs to keep his family afloat.
The groundswell of support kept his campaign afloat.
We only just manage to keep afloat on my husband's small salary.

aide.definition: n. someone who acts as assistant
aide.translation: n. 助手, 副官\n[计] 数据输入的可说明性

examples.en: The aide suggested a change in tactics to him.
I don't have an aide to help me.
The dictator had the absolute loyalty of all his aides.

ail.translation: vt. 使苦恼\nvi. 生病, 处境困难\n[计] 数组互联逻辑

examples.en: O what can ail thee, knight-at-arms, alone and palely loitering?
Yanni left to Algiers to take care of his ailing mother.
Full respect to Casper for completing the match while clearly ailing.

alcoholic.definition: n. a person who drinks alcohol to excess habitually\na. characteristic of or containing alcohol\ns. addicted to alcohol
alcoholic.translation: n. 酒鬼, 酒精中毒者\na. 酒精的

examples.en: People who drink alcoholic beverages are not allowed to enter.
examples.zh: 饮酒者不准禁入。

examples.en: His alcoholic neighbor lent him some money.
examples.zh: 他的一个酒鬼邻居，借给他了一笔钱。

examples.en: My mother was an alcoholic.
examples.zh: 我母亲是个酒鬼。

alienate.definition: v. make withdrawn or isolated or emotionally dissociated
alienate.translation: vt. 使疏远, 离间, 转让\n[法] 转让, 让与, 疏远

examples.en: How long have you been alienated from your family?
examples.zh: 你离开家有多久了?

examples.en: His coolness has alienated his friends.
examples.zh: 他冷酷的性格使朋友们一个一个地疏远了他。

examples.en: He felt alienated from society.
examples.zh: 他觉得被社会遗弃了。

alleged.definition: s. declared but not proved\ns. doubtful or suspect
alleged.translation: a. 被断言的, 所谓的\n[法] 提出而尚未证实的, 声称的, 宣称的

examples.en: The boss is alleged to have hit a worker.
That man is alleged to have committed the murder.
Recently, he's come under fire for alleged tax fraud.

allergy.definition: n. hypersensitivity reaction to a particular allergen; symptoms can vary greatly in intensity
allergy.translation: n. 变应性, 反感, 厌恶\n[化] 变态反应; 变应性

examples.en: Peanut allergy is the most common of food allergies.
examples.zh: 花生过敏是最常见的食物过敏。

examples.en: Constantly blowing his nose in allergy season.
examples.zh: 在过敏的季节不断地擤他的鼻子.

examples.en: I have an allergy to milk.
examples.zh: 我对牛奶过敏。

almighty.translation: a. 万能的, 全能的

examples.en: God is almighty and does what He wants to do.
May God Almighty deign to hear and grant our prayers.
May Almighty God graciously hear and answer our prayers.

alphabet.definition: n. a character set that includes letters and is used to write a language
alphabet.translation: n. 字母\n[计] 字母表

examples.en: How many letters are there in the alphabet?
examples.zh: 英文字母中有几个字母?

examples.en: I remember my mother teaching me the alphabet.
examples.zh: 我记得我母亲教我认字。

examples.en: If I could rearrange the alphabet, I would put U and I together.
examples.zh: 如果我可以把英文字母重新排序，我会把「U」和「I」放在一起。

alphabetic.definition: a. relating to or expressed by a writing system that uses an alphabet\na. arranged in order according to the alphabet
alphabetic.translation: a. 按字母次序的, 字母的

examples.en: I take part of the alphabetic mafia.
Alphabetic script on signs on streets and buildings is just boring, some think.

amiable.translation: a. 亲切的, 和蔼可亲的\n[法] 亲和的, 和蔼可亲的

examples.en: She is not only beautiful but also amiable.
The reason for my return is that the people of Chile are extraordinarily amiable.
Tom is an amiable chap.
One should not be scared of poverty, and instead, be determined amidst it.
examples.zh: 人不要怕穷，要穷中立志.

amongst.definition:
prep. Mixed or mingled; surrounded by.
prep. Conjoined, or associated with, or making part of the
   number of; in the number or class of.
prep. Expressing a relation of dispersion, distribution,
   etc.; also, a relation of reciprocal action.
amongst.translation: prep. 在...当中, 在...之间, 在...之中

examples.en: True art of life is to see the extraordinary amongst the ordinary.
examples.zh: 生活真正的艺术是在平凡中看到不平凡。

examples.en: He is the youngest amongst us four.
examples.zh: 他是我们四人中间最年轻的。

examples.en: He's the tallest amongst the boys.
examples.zh: 他算是男孩子中最高的了。

amplification.definition: n. addition of extra material or illustration or clarifying detail\nn. the amount of increase in signal power or voltage or current expressed as the ratio of output to input\nn. (electronics) the act of increasing voltage or power or current
amplification.translation: n. 扩大, 放大\n[化] 放大; 放大作用

examples.en: Social media leads to the amplification of once-fringe views, for better or worse.
Workers are installing extra loudspeakers because the music in tonight's concert will need amplification.
The amplification of DNA via PCR is a necessary step for many kinds of tests.

amusing.definition: s. providing enjoyment; pleasantly entertaining\ns. arousing or provoking laughter
amusing.translation: a. 有趣的, 引人发笑的

examples.en: She read an amusing story to the children.
examples.zh: 她给孩子们读了个有趣的故事。

examples.en: The story was amusing.
examples.zh: 故事很有趣。

examples.en: Foreign people are amusing.
examples.zh: 外国人很好玩。

ancestry.definition: n. inherited properties shared with others of your bloodline
ancestry.translation: n. 祖先, 世系, 名门出身

examples.en: However, the singer does not deny her ancestry.
examples.zh: 但是歌手并不否认她的出身。

anchorage.definition:
n. the condition of being secured to a base
n. a fee for anchoring
n. a city in south central Alaska
n. place for vessels to anchor
anchorage.translation: n. 下锚, 锚地, 停泊税\n[化] 固着; 固定; 锚定

examples.en: I'm going to Europe by way of Anchorage next week.
Anchorage is the northernmost big city in the US.
I went to Europe by way of Anchorage.

anew.definition: r again but in a new or different way

examples.en: When something comes to an end, you can start anew.
Love blinds, marriage allows one to find vision anew.
Now there’s no time to start anew.

anguish.definition: n. extreme mental distress\nn. extreme distress of body or mind\nv. suffer great pains or distress
anguish.translation: n. 剧痛, 痛苦\nvt. 使极痛苦\nvi. 感到痛苦

examples.en: She takes a new lover while he is in anguish.
The source of my anguish is your lack of loyalty.
I will speak in the anguish of my spirit.

antagonism.definition: n. the relation between opposing principles or forces or factors\nn. an actively expressed feeling of dislike and hostility\nn. (biochemistry) interference in or inhibition of the physiological action of a chemical substance by another having a similar structure
antagonism.translation: n. 对立, 敌对, 敌意\n[化] 拮抗作用; 消效作用

examples.en: The Cold War is the symbol of the antagonism between communism and capitalism.
Their ancient antagonism was rekindled.

antagonist.definition: n. a muscle that relaxes while another contracts\nn. a drug that neutralizes or counteracts the effects of another drug
antagonist.translation: n. 敌手, 对手\n[化] 对抗物; 拮抗物; 反协同剂; 反协同试剂

examples.en: The antagonist of the book was introduced on the second page.
Despite being the antagonist in the movie, I liked her character.
I'm usually more interested in films' antagonists than their protagonists.

antagonistic.definition: s. indicating opposition or resistance\ns. characterized by antagonism or antipathy\na. arousing animosity or hostility
antagonistic.translation: a. 对抗的, 敌对的\n[化] 拮抗药

examples.en: Buddhists seem less antagonistic towards science than are Christians.
The two countries are antagonistic to each other.
The emotional qualities are antagonistic to clear reasoning.

antagonistically.translation: adv. 敌对地, 对抗性地

antonym.definition: n. a word that expresses a meaning opposed to the meaning of another word, in which case the two words are antonyms of each other

examples.en: The word ‘antonym’ is antonymous to ‘synonym’.
examples.zh: 反义词这个单词是同义词的反义词

apologetic.translation: a. 道歉的, 急于认错的, 辩护的\n[法] 辩护的, 辩解的, 道歉的

examples.en: Tom was not apologetic.
examples.zh: Tom并不觉得抱歉。

appal.definition: v strike with disgust or revulsion\nv fill with apprehension or alarm; cause to be unpleasantly surprised
appal.translation: vt. 使惊骇, 使吓坏

examples.en: I was appalled by her lack of good manners.
I am shocked and appalled at what I have just seen.
Every time I see those pictures, I'm appalled.

appall.definition: v strike with disgust or revulsion\nv fill with apprehension or alarm; cause to be unpleasantly surprised
appall.translation: vt. 使丧胆, 使惊骇

examples.en: It constantly appalls me how stupid he can be.

appalling.definition: n. an experience that appalls\ns. causing consternation
appalling.translation: a. 骇人的, 令人震惊的

examples.en: There's an appalling shortage of phone booths in this area.
Even nowadays, a lot of people live in appalling conditions.
What you did is appalling, I can't believe it.

appealing.definition: a. able to attract interest or draw favorable attention
appealing.translation: a. 有感染力的, 动人的, 恳求的

examples.en: Financial security can be appealing to girls in relationships.
The locals are in the habit of wearing very appealing clothing.
Algiers has an appealing botanical garden named "Jardin d'Essai."

appease.definition: v cause to be more favorably inclined; gain the good will of\nv overcome or allay\nv make peace with
appease.translation: vt. 抚慰, 缓解, 平息, 姑息\n[法] 使和缓, 使满足, 姑息

examples.en: Management tried to appease labor by offering them a bonus.
Ravenswood pleaded, apologised, and even kneeled, to appease her displeasure.
The Algerian government is seeking to appease the masses.

appeasement.definition: n. the act of appeasing (as by acceding to the demands of)
appeasement.translation: n. 抚慰, 缓解, 平息, 姑息\n[法] 缓和:缓静, 安抚

examples.en: Appeasement must always trump confrontation.

appraise.definition: v evaluate or estimate the nature, quality, ability, extent, or significance of\nv consider in a comprehensive way
appraise.translation: vt. 评价, 估价\n[经] 评价, 鉴定

examples.en: "I have a guy coming later to appraise some antiques."
Tom had the painting appraised by an expert before he bought it.
An expert appraised the value of the watch as two hundred dollars.

aptitude.translation: n. 资质, 才能, 自然倾向\n[医] 资质, 才能

examples.en: He has a remarkable aptitude for music.
examples.zh: 他有非凡的音乐天份。

aptly.definition: r with competence; in a competent capable manner
aptly.translation: adv. 适当地, 适宜地

examples.en: It is aptly said that illness starts from the mind.
It is aptly said that necessity is the mother of invention.
Junk food, like twinkies are aptly named junk food, but still delicious.

arbitrate.definition: v act between parties with a view to reconciling differences
arbitrate.translation: vt. 仲裁, 公断\nvi. 进行仲裁

examples.en: They need to arbitrate this case.
Joseph will arbitrate the game.

arbitration.definition: n. (law) the hearing and determination of a dispute by an impartial referee agreed to by both parties (often used to settle disputes between labor and management)\nn. the act of deciding as an arbiter; giving authoritative judgment
arbitration.translation: n. 仲裁, 公断\n[计] 仲裁

examples.en: With arbitration, judgement is usually passed in six months' time.
If you agree to binding arbitration, you may forfeit some of your rights.
Counselling or arbitration is often the best way to solve disputes among members of the public.

argumentative.definition: a. given to or characterized by argument
argumentative.translation: a. 好辩的, 引起争论的, 论证式的\n[法] 争辩的, 辩论的, 有争议的

examples.en: To say that Tom was argumentative would be an understatement.
Tom gets very argumentative with a few beers under his belt.
Ziri is the most argumentative person I know.

aristocracy.definition: n a privileged class holding hereditary titles\nn the most powerful members of a society
aristocracy.translation: n. 贵族, 上层社会, 知识界杰出分子\n[法] 贵族政治, 贵族统治

examples.en: Mary's butler is the envy of the country's aristocracy.
An aristocrat is a member of the aristocracy.
Nancy comes from what we call the aristocracy.

aristocrat.definition: n. a member of the aristocracy

examples.en: Aristocrats lived to the east and west of the imperial palace.
examples.zh: 贵族住在故宫的东边和西边。

aristocratic.definition: s. belonging to or characteristic of the nobility or aristocracy
aristocratic.translation: a. 贵族的, 主张贵族统绐的, 有贵族气派的

examples.en: An aristocratic title is only inherited via the male lineage.
So much blood has been spilled over meaningless aristocratic quarrels.
Yuri grew up in an old reclusive aristocratic family.

arrogance.definition: n. overbearing pride evidenced by a superior manner toward inferiors
arrogance.translation: n. 傲慢态度, 自大

examples.en: I lost my temper with him because of his arrogance.
examples.zh: 我为他傲慢自大对他发火。

examples.en: I can't put up with his arrogance.
examples.zh: 我不能忍受他的傲慢。

examples.en: I cannot put up with his arrogance.
examples.zh: 我不能忍受他的傲慢。

artifact.definition: n. a man-made object taken as a whole
artifact.translation: n. 人工制品\n[医] 人为现象, 人工产物

examples.en: I heard they found an alien artifact on the moon.
The Artifact on the show "Picard" is an abandoned Borg cube.
Bennu is a primordial artifact preserved in the vacuum of space.

artistic.definition: a. relating to or characteristic of art or artists\ns. satisfying aesthetic standards and sensibilities
artistic.translation: a. 艺术的, 艺术家的, 富有艺术性的

examples.en: He was raised in an artistic family.
examples.zh: 他在艺术世家长大。

examples.en: In addition, she has an artistic flair.
examples.zh: 此外，她有艺术家天赋。

examples.en: My father is far from artistic.
examples.zh: 我父亲一点也不懂艺术。

assassin.definition: n. a murderer (especially one who kills a prominent political figure) who kills by a surprise attack and often is hired to do the deed\nn. a member of a secret order of Muslims (founded in the 12th century) who terrorized and killed Christian Crusaders
assassin.translation: n. 暗杀者, 刺客\n[法] 暗杀者, 行刺者

examples.en: Chigurh, a professional assassin, operates with a sense of calculated detachment.
Jonas hired the best assassin in the prison.
The assassin smothered his victim with a pillow.

assorted.definition: s. consisting of a haphazard assortment of different kinds\ns. of many different kinds purposefully arranged but lacking any uniformity
assorted.translation: a. 各种各样的, 分类的

examples.en: Tom gave Mary a box of assorted chocolates.
The butcher shop sells assorted cuts of meat.
This box contains assorted chocolates.

assortment.definition: n. a collection containing a variety of sorts of things
assortment.translation: n. 分类, 各种各样\n[医] [遗传]配列

examples.en: Here you'll find a wide assortment of high-quality security solutions.
An assortment of ripe fruit is on the table.
A clocktower is full of an assortment of doodads and doohickies.

astray.definition: r. away from the right path or direction
astray.translation: adv. 迷途地, 入歧途地\n[法] 误入歧途地, 离开正道地

examples.en: Better to ask the way than go astray.
examples.zh: 问路总比误入歧途好。

examples.en: The little girl will go astray if no one cares much about her.
examples.zh: 这小女孩如果没人关心的话，就要走上歪路了。

examples.en: We went astray in the woods.
examples.zh: 我们在树林中迷路了。

atmospheric.definition: a. relating to or located in the atmosphere
atmospheric.translation: a. 大气的\n[医] 大气的; 大气压的

examples.en: Venus' atmospheric pressure is very high.
examples.zh: 金星的大气压力非常高。

examples.en: The barometer is an instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, especially used to study climate and to determine altitudes.
examples.zh: 气压表是一种用来测量大气压力的仪器，主要用于研究气候和测量高度。

atop.definition: r. on, to, or at the top
atop.translation: adv. 在顶上\nprep. 在...的顶上

examples.en: The creature had a pair of antlers atop its head.
The crow perched atop the old oak tree, cawing loudly.
Kalman saw a massive creature with antlers atop its head.

atrocious.definition: s. shockingly brutal or cruel\ns. exceptionally bad or displeasing\ns. provoking horror
atrocious.translation: a. 残暴的, 凶恶的

examples.en: This is atrocious weather.
examples.zh: 恶劣的天气。

atrocity.definition: n. the quality of being shockingly cruel and inhumane\nn. an act of atrocious cruelty
atrocity.translation: n. 残暴, 凶恶, 暴行\n[法] 暴行, 残酷, 残忍

examples.en: Atrocity crimes are imminent unless there is a cessation of hostilities.
Daesh terrorists left a trail of atrocities in their wake.
It is hard to believe that humans are capable of such atrocity.

attendant.definition:
n. someone who waits on or tends to or attends to the needs of another
n. a person who is present and participates in a meeting
s. being present (at meeting or event etc.) "attendant members of the congreation"
s. following or accompanying as a consequence
attendant.translation: n. 随从, 侍者, 出席者\na. 侍候的, 伴随的, 出席的, 在场的

examples.en: Tom is a flight attendant.
examples.zh: 汤姆是空服员。

attentive.definition: a. (often followed by `to') giving care or attention
attentive.translation: a. 注意的, 留心的

examples.en: You're so attentive.
examples.zh: 你好细心。

auctioneer.definition: n. an agent who conducts an auction

examples.en: The auctioneer spoke too fast to be understood.
Tom used to work as an auctioneer.
Ziri observed the auctioneer with keen interest.

auditing.definition: v examine carefully for accuracy with the intent of verification\nv attend academic courses without getting credit
auditing.translation: [计] 审查, 审计处理\n[经] 查帐, 审计学

examples.en: The IRS is auditing me.
I'm auditing the course.

authoritative.definition: s. having authority or ascendancy or influence\ns. of recognized authority or excellence\ns. sanctioned by established authority
authoritative.translation: a. 权威性的, 官方的, 命令式的\n[法] 官方的, 当局的, 权威的

examples.en: Simpson's authoritative rule is bringing an end to our long-cherished federalism.
The Babylonian Talmud is considered more authoritative than the Jerusalemite Talmud.
He was the most authoritative among the people.

autobiographic.definition: a of or relating to or characteristic of an autobiographer\na relating to or in the style of an autobiography
autobiographic.translation: a. 自传的, 自传体的

automate.definition: v make automatic or control or operate automatically
automate.translation: vt.vi. (使)自动化\n[计] 自动化

examples.en: Each day our life becomes more comfortable and more automated.
examples.zh: 我们的生活日益变得更舒适更自动化。

examples.en: This is an automated payphone; you use it by inserting a coin.
examples.zh: 这是自动投币电话，用一元硬币来打的。

auxiliary.definition: s. functioning in a supporting capacity
auxiliary.translation: n. 辅助者, 辅助物, 附属机构, 助动词\na. 辅助的, 备用的

examples.en: 'can' is an auxiliary verb, so in question sentences it is brought to the start of the phrase.
examples.zh: 因为 can 是助动词，在疑问句中被放到了句首。

avail.definition:
n. a means of serving
v. use to one's advantage
v. be of use to, be useful to
v. take or use
avail.translation: vi. 有用, 有利\nvt. 有利于\nn. 效用, 利益

examples.en: You should avail yourself of every opportunity.
examples.zh: 你应该好好利用一切的机会。

examples.en: He was glad to avail himself of any means to succeed in life.
examples.zh: 他很高兴能通过各种方法在人生中取得成功。

examples.en: Crying is of no avail.
examples.zh: 哭是无济于事的。

availability.definition: n the quality of being at hand when needed
availability.translation: n. 有效性, 可利用性, 可利用的人\n[计] 有效性; 可用性

examples.en: Availability may vary by region and device compatibility.
examples.zh: 实际提供内容可能因地区与装置相容性而异。

avenge.definition: v take revenge for a perceived wrong

examples.en: He killed him in order to avenge his father's death.
examples.zh: 他杀了他，以为他父亲的死报仇。

examples.en: You killed my father. Today I will avenge him.
examples.zh: 你杀了我父亲，我今天要为他报仇。

examples.en: He killed him to avenge his dead father.
examples.zh: 他杀死了他，为死去的父亲报了仇。

aversion.definition: n. the act of turning yourself (or your gaze) away
aversion.translation: n. 厌恶, 讨厌的事, 讨厌的人\n[医] 厌恶, 移转, 移位

examples.en: My attraction to you has changed into aversion.
I feel an aversion toward all this exhibitionism.
I developed an aversion toward the word "awesome".

axe.definition: v. chop or split with an ax
axe.translation: n. 斧, 斧头\nvt. 削减(人员、经费、计划、机构等)

examples.en: Ziri heard the sound of an axe hitting a tree.
It's a sharp axe, but the branch is not yielding.
Karl used an axe to free himself from the chains.

accountable.definition: s. liable to account for one's actions
accountable.translation: a. 负有责任的, 可说明的, 可解释的\n[经] 负有责任的

examples.en: Legal frameworks exist to hold war criminals accountable.
examples.zh: 法律架构的存在，使战争罪犯的责任可以追究。

examples.en: Tom is accountable to me.
examples.zh: 汤姆要向我负责。

afterwards.definition: r happening at a time subsequent to a reference time

examples.en: Keep your eyes wide open before marriage, half shut afterwards.
examples.zh: 婚前张开眼，婚后半闭眼。

examples.en: I fixed my car last month, but it broke again afterwards.
examples.zh: 我的车我上个月修好了，后来又坏了。

examples.en: In addition, we will issue the 'employee of the month' award afterwards.
examples.zh: 另外，之后我们会颁发“每月最佳员工”奖。

air conditioning.translation: 用空调设备调节空气, 空调设备\n[计] 空调; 空气调节

examples.en: The opposition is just a bunch of antiquated politicians.
These sentences are useless because they are antiquated.
I am considered as an antiquated individual.

assassination.definition: n. murder of a public figure by surprise attack
assassination.translation: n. 暗杀\n[法] 暗杀, 行刺

examples.en: The FBI thwarted an assassination attempt against Mayor Matt Brown.
Yesterday, Algeria celebrated the 58th anniversary of Mouloud Feraoun's assassination.
Every March 15, Algeria celebrates the anniversary of Mouloud Feraoun's assassination.

austerity.definition: n. the trait of great self-denial (especially refraining from worldly pleasures)
austerity.translation: n. 朴素, 苦行, 严格, 严峻

examples.en: We've realised that our programme of austerity was completely barmy.
The fiscal austerity may lead to an overkill of the economy.
We realised that our austerity cuts were a totally daft idea.

averse.translation: a. 不愿意的, 反对的

examples.en: I am constitutionally averse to getting carried away with feelings.
He believed the superstition that Christians were averse to learning.
I'm not averse to a good night out.

acceleration.definition: n. an increase in rate of change\nn. the act of accelerating; increasing the speed\nn. (physics) a rate of increase of velocity
acceleration.translation: n. 加速, 促进, 加速度\n[化] 加速度

examples.en: My only critique for my car was its acceleration.
If not, how do you explain the acceleration?
The derivatives of space with respect to time are velocity, acceleration, and jerk.

acquisitive.definition: a. eager to acquire and possess things especially material possessions or ideas
acquisitive.translation: a. 渴望获得的, 贪婪的\n[法] 取得的, 获得的, 贪得无厌的

examples.en: He is acquisitive of knowledge.
examples.zh: 他很有求知欲。

adjustable.definition: s. capable of being changed so as to match or fit\ns. capable of being regulated
adjustable.translation: a. 可调节的\n[电] 可调整的
